We're putting together video interviews that may be shared with local officials, at community meetings, and through our YouTube and Instagram channels, with participants' permission. portable-restroom-septic-and-vac-truck-o.author: Arthur Tutt
portable-restroom-septic-and-vac-truck-o.core: Posted in last 7 days Portable Restroom, Septic & Vac Truck Operators - Sanitation Stories Hi my name is Arthur and I have a confession: I’ve inspected some pretty rad sewers in my life. Nothing builds humility and character quite like doing jobs that just gotta get done. It takes a brave few, and if you know, you know. I wanted to hear the stories of the hardworking operators out there that keep our world clean. The portable restroom operators, the septic operators, the vac truck operators, the people focused on bringing dignified sanitation to the world. I had a mic, a webcam, and a LinkedIn account, and with that, The Backbone podcast was born (start humble, stay hungry). Almost 1 year and 45 episodes later, the people I've met on this journey keep blowing me away. The scrappy, fearless entrepreneurs, the problem solvers, the misfits who blazed their own trail, the people who hustle evenings and weekends to support their families and build their dreams. These people make things happen. People who aren’t afraid of other people’s judgement, and show up because there’s a job that just needs to get done. My kind of people. If you don’t know me yet (hi!), here’s the quick origin story: My first co-op job as a naive, bright-eyed Guelph engineering student in 2009 was inspecting sewers in the Waterloo / Guelph area in Canada. There were concerns of too much rain water infiltrating through cracks and broken pipes, and it was our job to find where (talk about a needle in a haystack…). After graduating in 2012 I moved abroad and spent 2 years in Manchester in the UK, building computer models of their sewer systems to identify flood concerns and where pipes needed to be resized for increased demand. In 2014 returned back to my hometown of Toronto and worked on an extensive basement flooding remediation project. It was a wild experience working in neighbourhoods I grew up in and knowing I was helping to solve recurring flooding problems in my community. I kinda felt like Batman, but for the sewers (or does that make me a ninja turtle??). Around 2017 it was time for a change. I packed my bags and went travelling around the world to do some soul searching. 10-day silent meditation retreats, dog sitting, and several career changes later, from running a digital marketing agency to being a hypnotherapist (yeah that happened), my day job now is developing software to help businesses automate workflows and build systems that connect the dots and keep teams organized. In evenings & weekends I’m a podcast host, talking to sanitation operators about the grit and resilience it takes to run a business in this industry. It’s been a wild ride. If you’re a portable restroom or septic operator and you’ve got stories to share and life experience from the trenches, reach out, I want to hear your story. Best, Arthur

And I’m already excited. As one of the NRF Retail Voices for 2027, I’ve been getting a behind-the-scenes peek at what’s planned. As usual, the programme is packed, exciting and informative, with conversations that matter for the year ahead. I’m already getting organised. When I first started travelling from Dublin to New York for NRF, people would ask whether a US retail show was worth the trip. What becomes clear when you’re there is just how global it is. People travel from all over the world to see the latest innovations, share perspectives and understand what’s shaping retail across markets. For me, that global perspective makes it an investment at the start of the retail year that I never regret. NRF sets the stage for the year ahead. It’s where I take the pulse of the industry: what retailers are prioritising, where investment is going and how new ideas are translating into practice. And as the global retail community becomes more connected, understanding what’s happening beyond our own markets matters more than ever. Three additions from National Retail Federation and Rethink Retail to put in the diary that are all taking place at Lavan in New York: 📍 Commerce Media Saturday Exploring how retail media is evolving across stores and online, and expanding into sectors such as financial services, travel and hospitality - https://lnkd.in/e7SJAe2t 📍 Supply Chain Sunday From inventory and availability to last-mile delivery and returns. So much of the shopper experience depends on what happens behind the scenes - https://lnkd.in/eJhsknGA 📍 AI Monday - AiR Summit & Soirée An opportunity to explore how AI is being applied across retail and what that means for the industry - https://lnkd.in/eMPXeNiZ Together, these touch on so much of what I’m interested in: how we help shoppers discover and choose, how we deliver on the promise, and how technology can support better outcomes. Then there are the people. Catching up with familiar faces within the community, making new connections and having those unplanned conversations that stay with you long after you get home. I'm also on the look out with Renee Hartmann for new retail stories to bring to the What's In Store - Making Sense of Modern Retail content series in 2027. If you’re heading to NRF, drop me a line.
